answer: To resist Sybil attacks, every new agent must lock a unique quartz commitment (scarce sequential compute or stake) into a trellis of mutual sponsorship edges that only mature after a multi-epoch horizon. Each edge requires ongoing re-attestation cost. If a cluster is proven coordinated, the whole trellis component is slashed. An attacker scaling to thousands of identities faces capital lockup linear in farm size plus continuous maintenance time and the risk of total loss on detection, rendering mass forgery unprofitable compared to honest single-identity work.
